findings.what: AC2 ("three settlements distinguished") is reported **done** citing "`already_settled` via the derivation cell + World leg 1", but World leg 1 is a reimbursement and NOTHING in the branch admits or posts an `already_settled` claim. The arm ships with zero regression protection and the report's evidence pointer is false.
findings.evidence: `grep -c 'already_settled\|alreadySettled'` → packages/db/tests/staff-expense-claim.test.mjs **0**, packages/runtime/tests/staff-expense-claim-e2e.mjs **0**, apps/web/components/accounting/staff-expense-claim-form.test.tsx **0**, apps/web/e2e/staff-expense-claim-walk.spec.ts **0**; only the two pure-shape unit files mention it (runtime 4, web-draft 4). `packages/runtime/tests/staff-expense-claim-e2e.mjs:270` is literally `settlement: "reimbursement"`. I proved the arm WORKS myself on the from-scratch chain (probe r638_probe1 on 55603/clara_638r): admit → 202 with claim_id, post → `{"posted":true}`, GL `[6200 dr 48000, 6210 dr 12500, 1150 cr 60500]`, ledger `["admitted","posted"]` — so this is unproven behaviour plus a wrong citation, not broken behaviour.
findings.fix: Add `p638.claim.settled` to packages/db/tests/staff-expense-claim.test.mjs: `claim({ settlement: SETTLEMENT.settled, payableAccountCode: null })` (the fixture already builds it — staff-expense-claim-fixtures.mjs:229), admit through the door, post via `wakeRecordJournalEntry` under the real interactive_client credential, and assert the three derived lines, exactly one committed receipt, one claim row and the `posted` ledger row. Then correct the AC2 evidence pointer in 638-final.md (World leg 1 is reimbursement).

findings.what: A claim dated into a closed/closing fiscal year is ADMITTED — a durable `clara.staff_expense_claims` row, Work and task — and refuses only at posting with CLR19. The cited sibling refuses it at ADMISSION (`clara._assert_adjustment_relationships`, arm "THE LOCKED PERIOD, TYPED AND EARLY", CLR19 `write_into_closed_period`). Because a claim, unlike a plain journal Work, writes a register row at admission, the result is a permanent, never-postable claim the register cannot distinguish from one still queued.
findings.evidence: Probe r638_probe4/P12 on the from-scratch rig (55603/clara_638r): after `seedFiscalYear(..., status:'closed')`, `admit_staff_expense_claim_work` returned `{work, claim}`; posting then refused `CLR19 {"reason":"write_into_closed_period"}`; `clara.list_staff_expense_claims` still returns the row with `entry_id:null, entry_status:null` and ledger `["admitted"]`. apps/web/components/accounting/staff-expense-claims-table.tsx:113-116 renders exactly that as the `history.admitted` badge forever. The branch's own cell (staff-expense-claim.test.mjs:533-543) asserts only `entryCount === 0` and never looks at the stranded row. `_assert_claim_basis`'s world half (0206:861-975) asks the chart, the enrolment and the advance cap but never `clara.fiscal_years`.
findings.fix: Add a world-half arm to `clara._assert_claim_basis`: look up the fiscal year covering `posting_date` and, when its status is `closing`/`closed`, raise CLR19 with `detail.reason='write_into_closed_period'`, `field='claim.posting_date'` — the same shape `_assert_adjustment_relationships` raises. Flip staff-expense-claim.test.mjs:533 to `refusesSec(...)` at admission (it would go red today). If the arm is deliberately left to the posting core instead, name the residual in the report and give the register a distinct face for a claim whose Work is refused/cancelled.

findings.what: Two concurrent corrections of one claim escape as a raw `23505`, not a typed refusal: `_assert_claim_basis`'s (iv) correction-target check (0206:948) runs before the client rung and under no row lock, and step 8's `on conflict` arbitrates `work_id` only, so the loser violates the partial unique index unhandled. `workErrorResponse` claims 40P01/40001 and CLR codes only, so the route answers HTTP 500 `{error:"internal"}` and the browser shows `kind:"unavailable"` instead of the `correction_target_already_corrected` the successor contract's refusal map promises. The posting core's own handler states the house rule: "never as a raw 23505 the runtime cannot classify".
findings.evidence: Probe r638_probe2/P5 on 55603/clara_638r: post a claim, `reverse_entry`, then hold `pg_advisory_xact_lock(203005004, hashtext(client))` from a third session as a barrier and fire two `clara.admit_staff_expense_claim_work` calls (different intent keys, same `corrects_claim_id`) as `clara_runtime`. A → 202; **B → `{"ok":false,"code":"23505","msg":"duplicate key value violates unique constraint \"uq_staff_expense_claims_corrects\""}`**. Data stayed correct (exactly one correction landed; the chain is linked both ways) — the defect is the untyped refusal, not corruption. workRoutes.ts:739-742 handles only 40P01/40001; sendAdmissionError (:835-843) falls through to 500.
findings.fix: In `clara.admit_staff_expense_claim_work`, after the client rung is taken (step 6), `perform 1 from clara.staff_expense_claims where id = v_corrects and client_id = p_client for update` and re-ask the (iv) checks under that lock; or wrap the step-8 insert in `exception when unique_violation then raise ... CLR10 detail.reason='correction_target_already_corrected'`. Add a red-first race cell beside `p638.advance.race`.

findings.what: AC4 is reported **done**, but the half the brief named — "the document released by `t_entry_evidence_release`" (brief-638.md §4 seam 11) — is not asserted anywhere. `p638.correction` passes no `sourceRefs`, and the World e2e's PASS 7 only proves the link is BORN inside the posting transaction.
findings.evidence: packages/db/tests/staff-expense-claim.test.mjs:669-718 builds its claims with no `sourceRefs`; `grep -n 'entry_evidence_links' packages/db/tests/staff-expense-claim.test.mjs` → no matches. packages/runtime/tests/staff-expense-claim-e2e.mjs:549-552 asserts `evLinks.rows.length === 1` and `attached_via === 'work_commit'` and never reverses. Untested consequence: after reversing a documented claim, the correction claim citing the same receipt meets `_document_posting_entry` → CLR13 `source_already_posted` unless the link was released, so AC4's unwind is unproven for the documented case.
findings.fix: Extend `p638.correction` (or add `p638.correction.evidence`) to admit the first claim with a filed document in `sourceRefs`, post it, `reverse_entry`, then assert the `clara.entry_evidence_links` row for that entry is released and that the correcting claim can cite the same document without CLR13.

findings.what: Merge-order hazard the orchestrator should plan for: §0 refuses to apply unless the `_subledger_on_approve` caller roster matches a byte-exact six-name string AND the six non-regression bodies match shas measured on a 0001→0198 chain. 0206 merges after 0199–0205, and the census regex `p.prosrc ~ 'clara\._subledger_on_approve *\('` scans every clara body — so a sibling that merely names the hook inside any function's source would fail 0206's prestate at integration rather than at review.
findings.evidence: 0206:259-273 (roster string) and :232-256 (six shas). DECISIONS §1.3 exempts all six bodies from every sibling's recut list, so the exposure is the roster string, not the shas. On my from-scratch 0001→0198+0206 chain both held: `#638 prestate: clean …` and `#638 tail OK (1/7)…(7/7)`.
findings.fix: At integration, apply the merged chain 0001→0209 from scratch once before release; if 0206's prestate refuses, re-measure and re-issue 0206's roster string rather than weakening the assertion.

findings.what: The fresh cluster is LEFT RUNNING for the fix round: `rig638r` on port **55603**, database `clara_638r` (194 migrations 0001→0206 applied from scratch, seeded, #638 battery 21/21). Also recording why the World leg could not be proven on a fresh database: the e2e's DSN gate requires `clara_(rt_test|wave_b_ci)`, and migrating a SECOND database in the same cluster fails at `0154_binding_proposal_pr_1` ("the clara role count moved from 14 to 18 -- this file mints no role") because Postgres roles are cluster-level, not per-database.
findings.evidence: `pg_lsclusters` shows `17 rig638r 55603 online`. The clara_rt_test attempt on 55603 logged `migrate: FAIL — migration 0154_binding_proposal_pr_1 failed and was rolled back: … role count moved from 14 to 18`, exit 1. Against that half-migrated db the e2e printed `[sec-e2e] SKIPPED — migration 0206 … is not on this database`, exit 0 (which does independently prove the skip-clean condition action.yml promises). I therefore re-ran the World e2e on the lane's own rig (55503/clara_rt_test): 7 legs, `STAFF EXPENSE CLAIM E2E: PASS`, exit 0, first attempt — an independent confirmation of the report's claim, but not from-scratch.
findings.fix: None for the branch. If a from-scratch World leg is wanted, build a dedicated cluster whose FIRST database is named `clara_rt_test`.
